scope: Build variants of the trunk electronics bay. cad/build.py reads MICRO_COMPUTE (default 'zero') and sizes the deck and the board envelope from the entry below. bay_mm is [X extent, Y extent] in the assembly frame, so a board lying with its long side across the robot is [short, long]. tools/electronics_fit.py checks the built bay against the declared outline.

boards.name: Radxa Zero 3W 4GB
boards.note: the board the official Microduck install targets; chosen by the owner as the first integrated candidate

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
boards.note: same outline, so the same bay takes it; different SoC and camera path

blocked_by: laid along X the 67 mm bay runs into the neck tube neck_link, which occupies x 13.6-38.4 from z 140.5 up
laid across Y it needs y +/-33.5 plus a 3 mm frame, and the trunk interior at deck height is only +/-29.7 there
dropped under the neck tube to z 136-138.5 it runs into the hip yaw servo, which reaches z 144.5 at x 0-14, y 14-21
zero.would_need: a wider trunk shell, the neck column moved, or the board carried in the head instead

boards.name: board to be selected
boards.note: the bay that builds clean. tools/bay_probe.py measures the largest free rectangle at the deck plane as 34 x 49 mm for the board itself; the 3 mm deck frame has to come out of that, which is why the opening is 26.5 x 47. No mainstream Linux SBC is this short: Radxa Zero 3W and Pi Zero 2 W are 65 x 30, CM4 and CM5 are 55 x 40 before a carrier.

not_offered.name: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 4GB
not_offered.why: 40 mm across collides with the neck horn plate at y 14.5-17.5. It needs the plate moved or a wider trunk, not just a bigger deck. Module outline excludes the carrier, which is larger again.

excluded_from_every_number: connectors, camera FFC, wiring loom, standoffs and cooling
finding: The documents committed to a Radxa Zero 3W before anything checked it against the trunk. tools/bay_probe.py then measured the trunk: the largest free rectangle at the deck plane is 34 x 49 mm, so no standard SBC fits. Carrying a Linux board is a body decision - a wider trunk, the board in the head, or a module on a custom carrier - not a parts decision.

tried_and_reverted.change: trunk widened from 90 x 77 to 104 x 104 mm so the 65 x 30 Radxa Zero 3W would fit
tried_and_reverted.result: the board fitted, and the robot got worse
why: the thigh spans y 43-75 and the widened body reached y 52, so the hip pitch sweep hit the flank; carving the real swept volume out removed most of the lower side of the body
raising the dome to fix the resulting saucer shape split the shell into two solids
the neck column runs vertically through the middle of the trunk, so a 65 mm board cannot span it and has to sit beside it, which is what forces the width
tried_and_reverted.conclusion: a standard Linux SBC does not go in this trunk. The remaining option worth measuring is the head, which is 108 x 110 x 62 mm and mostly empty, at the cost of backward tipping margin.
